title: kv-cache: improve memory management and eviction (defrag, paging, spillover heuristics)
author: Alex Chen
description:
Motivation: Under sustained multi-tenant workloads we observed increased OOMs and degraded tail latency due to fragmented KV cache allocations and heavy spillover to host memory. This PR implements a series of memory-management improvements and eviction heuristics to reduce fragmentation, make spillover/paging behavior more predictable, and prioritize eviction to maintain tail-latency SLOs.

Summary of changes: Implements a compacting slab allocator for short-lived KV entries and a background defragmentation worker, introduces a spillover paging path to controlled host-backed arenas, and refines eviction priority to consider sequence locality, access recency, and pinned-session weights. Adds metrics and tracing for fragmentation, spillover rate, and compaction work. Includes unit and e2e tests plus benchmarks showing reduced OOMs and improved p99 latency under pressure.

Design notes: - Memory allocator: replace greedy variable-sized arena allocation with a slab/bucket allocator for the common small-entry case (<= 8KB). Large entries still use a dedicated arena with alignment. This reduces internal fragmentation and speeds allocation under contention. - Defragmentation: a cooperative background compactor runs on GPU host threads when node memory utilization > 65% and a fragmentation ratio exceeds 12%. Compaction operates per-shard to bound pause times and uses rate limiting to avoid competing with inference work. - Spillover paging: when device resident memory is exhausted, we now move low-priority KV shards to a host-backed spillover arena (pinned host page cache) with asynchronous prefetch. The spill path is conservative: we only spill entries which haven't been accessed in the last N requests (configurable), and we maintain a small hot-resident window to avoid high fetch rates. - Eviction heuristic: combine recency (LRU-ish), sequence-locality score (favor evicting entries spanning many different sequences), and pinned-session weight (do not evict pinned complaint entries). The heuristic uses a tunable score formula so ops teams can prioritize latency vs unit-cost. - Observability: new per-shard metrics: kv_fragmentation_ratio, kv_spill_rate, kv_compaction_time_ms, kv_evictions_by_reason. Traces include compactor traces and host-prefetch spans.

Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks show 18-25% reduction in memory overhead on mixed-length sequence workloads and ~30% fewer OOM incidents in our perf-canary synthetic tenancy test. Under a 10k qps multi-tenant mix, p99 generation latency decreased from 280ms to 240ms during sustained memory pressure in canary runs. CI includes unit tests for allocator invariants, integration test that verifies correctness of spill/prefetch under race, and a perf harness job that compares baseline vs this change.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged default off; gated rollout to dedicated pools for 2 weeks, then enable for select hosted regions with increased observability retention. Feature flag and tuning knobs exposed in runtime config: kv.defrag.enabled, kv.spill.enabled, kv.eviction.tuning.*.

Related: ENG-2841 (kv OOM incidents), ENG-2897 (tail latency under memory pressure).
commits:
Commit summary:
- Add slab allocator and bucket sizing strategy for small KV entries (runtime/kv/allocator.{cc,h})
- Implement shard-level background defragmentation worker with rate limiting (runtime/kv/defrag.{cc,h})
- Add host-backed spillover arena and async prefetch path (runtime/kv/spillover.{cc,h})
- Eviction policy engine refactor to support composite scoring and pinned-session weights (runtime/kv/evict.{cc,h})
- Expose tuning knobs and feature flags (runtime/config/kv.yaml)
- Add metrics, tracing hooks and perf harness updates (observability/kv_metrics.{cc,h}, benchmarks/kv_spillover_bench)
- Unit & integration tests (tests/kv_alloc_tests.cc, tests/kv_spillover_integration.cc)
review_comments:
Samir Patel (reviewer): Please add more detail on compaction safety — what prevents moving entries required by in-flight inference?

Author (Alex Chen): Compactor operates only on unpinned entries and acquires a brief per-shard allocation lock; moving an entry uses a two-phase swap with a tombstone marker so in-flight readers either see old or new location but never invalid memory. Added comments and a unit test that simulates a racing inference and compaction sequence.

Marta Ruiz (reviewer): The spill prefetch latency looks concerning; can we make prefetch aggressive for hot sequences?

Author (Alex Chen): Prefetch aggressiveness is tunable; default conservatively backoffs. We added an adaptive prefetch policy that increases prefetch budget for shards with rising access rate, and we instrumented prefetch hit-rate.

Diego Alvarez (approver): Verified metrics and smoke perf. sgtm with minor nits (logging levels).
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: slab allocator, background defragmentation, host spillover with async prefetch, and refined eviction heuristics. Reduces OOMs and improves tail latency during memory pressure. Feature-flagged and configurable.
